title: God of the Prophets' Power
description: God of the Prophets' Power in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 168, “The Word of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of the pro-phets' power! God of the go-spel's sound! Move glo-rious on, send out Thy voice To all the na-tions round.

lines: Move glorious on, — send out Thy voice
We bless Thee for Thy word;
We praise Thee for the joyful news
May neither fowls, nor rocks, nor thorns,
And though we sow in tears,
Our souls at last shall come,
And gather in our sheaves with joy,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
